A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same joint causal-discovery and representation-learning framework, renamed from NCDL to CaDRe. All 32 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, figures and tables, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original simulations of graph and latent-variable recovery, CESM2 forecasting results, and climate-graph visualizations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original simulations, quantitative wind-alignment comparisons, and forecasting results across climate and other time-series domains.

M1.justification: The two-encoder VAE, flow priors, Jacobian-based graph recovery and principal loss weights remain. However, v2's stated graph-extraction equation omits the separately learned mask used in v1 (Appendix C.2), retaining the spatial mask and threshold. Appendix E.2.3 also proposes an adaptation using adjacent-observation windows and temporal masking, presented as a potential extension.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained CESM2 forecasting and WeatherBench wind comparisons, v2 evaluates Jena Weather and ERSST forecasting, plus ILI, electricity-consumption and road-traffic forecasting (Appendix D.2). It also tests second-order latent dynamics, substantially broadening the evaluated domains and temporal scenarios.

E2.justification: The CESM2 forecasting comparison adds Timer-XL, TimeMixer, TimeXer and xLSTM-Mixer. New comparisons include PC, TCDF and IDOL for climate graph recovery, and Informer, PatchTST, DLinear, DLinear+FAN and N-Transformer for Weather forecasting. The retained sample-size comparison and Table 2 retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: v2 introduces WSHD/WTPR wind-alignment metrics, SMCC physical-variable alignment and graph-inference latency evaluation, extends dimensionality sweeps, and adds forecasting horizons and second-order simulation protocols. Its new simulation equations specify uniform observational noise with autoregressive dependence, while Gaussian-noise prose is retained; this reported specification conflict does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 extends scalability analyses to masked observational dimensions 20, 50, 80 and 200, adds second-order latent-dynamics tests, and expands the physical interpretation case study in Figure 5. Table A11 expands ablation metrics and replaces v1's orthogonal latent-transition test with an orthogonal observation-mapping test labelled a latent-drift violation. Existing latent-dimension and hyperparameter-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Five-seed simulation reporting remains. v2 newly states that real-world results are averaged over three random seeds and adds standard deviations to retained injectivity and generation-variability ablation results (v1 Table 7 versus v2 Table A11). These are reporting additions, not evidence of increased run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial forecasting, scalability, ablation and higher-order results. Its new CESM2 graph comparison reports CaDRe WSHD 0.012 and WTPR 0.532 (Table 3). Table 2 and the original CESM2 forecasting scores remain unchanged. Some newly reported results conflict internally: Timer-XL's CESM2-96 MAE is 0.425 in Table 4 but 0.497 in Table A16.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 adds a differentiability assumption and a differentiable latent-recovery conclusion. Appendix A.3 adds transition variability and a latent causal-graph identifiability conclusion. Appendix E.1 formalizes the higher-order extension briefly asserted in v1, while E.2 introduces a four-measurement model, limited-feedback assumptions and derivations for lagged observed effects. Much of the original SEM–ICA reasoning is retained.

C1.justification: Joint nonparametric identification of latent processes and observed causal structure remains the central contribution. v2 removes v1's explicit claim to be the first framework simultaneously tackling CRL and CD, and foregrounds competitive forecasting and physical interpretation of recovered latent drivers. The core research objective remains stable.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking recovered precipitation, solar radiation, cloud cover and delayed humidity effects (Section 5.2), alongside new discussion of applicability to other domains. Appendix B.3 explicitly identifies observed-to-latent causation as unsupported. The new climate-only evaluation limitation in Section 6 conflicts with the non-climate experiments in Table A15.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation through explicit simulation equations, architecture dimensions and activations in Table A7, disclosure of a MICN encoder backbone for real-world data, additional dataset access and downsampling information, and a least-squares description of spatial initialization. These disclosures do not establish that every newly described component changed between implementations.

R1.justification: Related work expands into separate climate-analysis, CRL, causal-discovery and forecasting discussions, with new positioning against IDOL and other methods in Appendix A.9. Added works include GraphCast, FourCastNet, Dong et al. (2023) and Lachapelle et al. (2024). The earlier linear latent-model survey is reduced; publication updates to retained works are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The title and method name change, theorem and lemma presentation is reorganized, experimental details and extended results are separated, and new discussion, ethics, reproducibility and disclosure sections are introduced. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are redesigned, Figure 4 gains a second row of dimensionality comparisons, and Figure 5 becomes a multi-time-point display combining latent and observed structures with wind fields. New comparison and architecture tables and lagged-model diagrams are added. Existing dimensionality results move into, and partly repeat across, appendix tables; the computational-cost plot is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful architecture and assumption details, quantitative wind validation and broader evaluation beyond v1's principally CESM2-based application. However, conflicting forecast values in Tables 4 and A16 and incompatible simulation-noise descriptions undermine the reliability and reproducibility of parts of the added evidence. These benefits and unresolved reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of the net overall quality change.
